thread:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — I'm sketching a proposal to move the policy resolver into a DI/plugin layer so we can inject per-tenant strategy implementations without rebuilding the runtime. Key idea: non-blocking fallback to legacy resolver when plugin lookup or init fails. sketch and tradeoffs below.

Alex Roberts: curious about perf — DI layer adds indirection. do we have numbers? :thinking:

Samir Patel: can we lazy-init plugins? warm vs cold start tradeoffs matter a lot for tail latency.

Lee Wong: +1 on lazy init. need explicit lifecycle hooks: init(ctx), shutdown(), healthCheck(). also a way to force-warm for Dedicated pools.

Maria Chen: quick perf note from a micro-bench — optimized path should be ~50-120ns extra per-decision if we avoid reflection and keep lookups in a tight map. worst-case (cold init + jar verification) is ms-scale, so must be async or gated. proposed pattern snippet: 

```
interface PolicyStrategy {
  Decision eval(Request r);
  void init(Context c);
}

// resolver uses DI to get PolicyStrategy for tenant
```

Priya Iyer: telemetry reqs: per-plugin exec_count, exec_latency_p50/p95/p99, error_count, fallback_count. tag metrics with tenant_id, model, route. we need spans for slow plugin in traces.

deploy-bot: canary created: infra/canaries/policy-resolver-di-prototype -> canary-3 (low-volume)

Alex Roberts: migration question: how do we handle existing compiled/legacy rules? do we convert them to plugins or run both stacks in parallel?

Maria Chen: migration plan draft: keep legacy path as default. enable DI lookup behind a feature flag. Start canary with a handful of internal tenants where plugin exists. If lookup returns null -> fallback to legacy synchronously; if plugin init fails -> mark unhealthy and fallback. Collect metrics, then expand.

Samir Patel: failure modes to consider: plugin init throws, plugin panics on eval, plugin blocks. resolver should: 1) catch panics, 2) circuit-break unhealthy plugin, 3) increment fallback metric, 4) ensure backoff before reattempting init. no request should be blocked waiting for plugin init beyond a short deadline.

Lee Wong: policy versioning note: plugin metadata must include schema_version and compatible_range. resolver should reject incompatible plugins at lookup time and return a clear diagnostic in logs/trace.

Priya Iyer: security constraints: for Private deployments we may allow customer-supplied plugins, but require signed bundles and KMS/HSM verification, plus static analysis scan in CI. add that to the rollout checklist.

Alex Roberts: tests: unit + sim tests are required. add a "dangling-plugin" sim (plugin that registers, then suddenly becomes unavailable) to ensure no goroutine/memory leaks and that fallback happens quickly. Also add perf harness to measure steady-state overhead.

Maria Chen: agreed. owners & next steps: Samir protos lazy-init + backoff (owner). Alex builds perf harness and sim tests. Priya specs telemetry + signing requirements. I'll write rollout plan, docs, and feature-flag gating. Target: prototype PR in ~2 weeks, internal canary in ~6 weeks.

Samir Patel: noted — will post PR/bench links here when available.

Lee Wong: sounds good, thanks all. :thumbsup:
